title: A Multiclass Quantum Aligned Centroid Kernel
abstract: Kernel methods are powerful tools in machine learning but commonly used full-Gram kernels face three key limitations: (1) quadratic scaling with training set size; (2) the use of fixed, non-trainable kernels; and (3) the absence of an intrinsic formulation for multiclass classification. We present McQuack, a trainable quantum kernel method for multiclass problems that achieves linear scaling in the number of training samples. This is accomplished by replacing the full training-set Gram matrix with a trainable sample-to-(class-centroid) fidelity matrix. We evaluate the model in simulation and on 124 qubits of two IBM devices, across more than 150 datasets. In simulation, McQuack outperforms existing "pure" quantum baselines, while results from hardware inference -- obtained without training -- achieve performance similar to an RBF kernel. Finally, we study the trainability of the model and observe no evidence of barren plateaus in our experiments with up to 13 qubits, and highlight the importance of parameter initialization for successful optimization.
summary: This paper introduces McQuack, a novel and efficient quantum kernel method designed for multiclass classification. It overcomes major bottlenecks in existing quantum kernel approaches by using a class-centroid fidelity matrix, achieving linear scaling with data size. The results demonstrate strong performance both in simulation and on real quantum hardware, while also confirming the model's trainability.
main_problem: The authors aim to develop an efficient, trainable quantum kernel method for multiclass classification that overcomes the quadratic scaling and fixed nature of traditional full-Gram kernels.
main_result: The proposed McQuack kernel achieves linear scaling in both training samples and classes, outperforming pure quantum baselines in simulation and matching RBF performance on hardware inference without explicit training.
method: McQuack replaces the full Gram matrix with a trainable sample-to-(class-centroid) fidelity matrix, allowing for shared parameters across all class classifiers.
model_or_system: The method is evaluated using quantum kernels defined by state fidelity $|\langle\psi_j|\psi_iangle|^2$, implemented on 124-qubit subgraphs of IBM quantum devices and simulated environments.
key_observables: Classification accuracy (compared to RBF kernel, SVC, MLP), training complexity ($O(n_{	ext{train}} M)$), and the absence of barren plateaus up to 13 qubits.
important_parameters: Training parameters ($\mathbf{w}, \mathbf{b}$) and class centroids ($\mathbf{c}_m$); hardware qubit count (up to 124).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that classes can be well-represented by centroids in the Hilbert space; training on actual quantum hardware is currently infeasible due to long runtimes.
figures_summary: Figure 12 illustrates the circuit architecture used to implement a quantum kernel measurement (probability of measuring the all-zero state).
paper_structure: The paper introduces McQuack, details its linear scaling mechanism using class centroids, provides theoretical background on QKMs and Kernel Target Alignment, evaluates performance in simulation against baselines, tests hardware inference, and analyzes trainability diagnostics.
why_interesting: It directly addresses the practical limitations of applying quantum computation to machine learning tasks by proposing a scalable, trainable kernel method suitable for near-term noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices.
